chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Dancer John Porcher introduces him to show business
summary: A friend, dancer John Porcher, took him to a club full of singers and dancers, his first exposure to show business.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And another friend of mine, Eugene, he began to really play snare drum very well, and like he lived close to me so we would always be together and he would show me things that I didn't understand. And so from that, after I left school, there was a friend of mine who was a dancer, and he asked -- he invited me, 'Come up to the club where we're dancing, and I would like you to see, you know, understand the different rhythms and things.'
So I said, 'Oh, I think that would be very interesting.'
So we went to the club.
John Porcher his name was, P-o-r-c-h-e-r.
Oh, he was also French background or something, wasn't he?
Uh-huh. Because I know some Porchers here.
And I often think of Johnny. He was a wonderful dancer.
About the same age as you?

Yeah, the same age, and a marvelous dancer. So I used to hang out with him a lot because he hung around musical people and dancers and singers, you know, in show business, which I was never introduced to show business before, and I thought it was something incredible. I never saw all these wonderful people singing and dancing. That just struck me. I said, 'Oh, God, this is where I want to be.'
